lm(N ~ time/resp - 1, Gabor) in MPDiR's inst/scripts/Ch6.R (code chunk 14, ClassImage.Stex), the classification image as the mean noise per time point and response class; the chunk before only averages N by time and resp with tapply, and the help page's example only runs str(Gabor).

glm(Response ~ log10(Contrast), binomial(mafc.logit(2)), StairCase) in MPDiR's inst/scripts/Ch5.R (code chunk 20, PsychFun2.Stex), then psyfun.2asym(cbind(Response, 1 - Response) ~ log10(Contrast)); the help page's example only plots Contrast on Trial.

panel.psyfun's glm(cbind(n * y, n * (1 - y)) ~ x, binomial(lnk)) of Pc on Phaseshift with n = 20 in each Direction, WaveForm and TempFreq panel, then glm(cbind(NumUpward, NumDownward) ~ Direction * WaveForm * TempFreq * Phaseshift, binomial, Vernier) with probit, cauchit and cloglog updates, in MPDiR's inst/scripts/Ch4.R (code chunks 20 to 22, PsychFun.Stex); NumUpward are the successes of the N trials per condition.

Bayes Rules! section 4.1 (https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-4) draws bechdel_20 <- bechdel %>% sample_n(20) and updates each analyst's Beta prior on pi, the share of movies that pass, by the Binomial count of binary == 'PASS' (Table 4.1); section 4.2 repeats it on the movies of 1991, 2000 and 2013 (filter(year == ...)). The help page has no examples and the package ships no script that uses bechdel.

stan_glm(rides ~ temp_feel, data = bikes, family = gaussian, prior_intercept = normal(5000, 1000), prior = normal(100, 40), prior_aux = exponential(0.0008)) in Bayes Rules! section 9.3.1 (https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-9), the book's first use of bikes; exercises 9.9 to 9.14 regress rides on humidity and windspeed.

stan_glm(laws ~ percent_urban + historical, data = equality, family = gaussian) on equality_index without California (filter(state != 'california')) in Bayes Rules! chapter 12's opening (https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-12), before the Poisson regression of laws on the same predictors.

Bayes Rules! section 5.3.3 (https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-5) keeps the 25 players with group == 'fb_concuss' and models their hippocampal volumes as Normal around mu with sigma = 0.5 under a Normal prior, plot_normal_likelihood(y = concussion_subjects$volume, sigma = 0.5); exercise 5.12 repeats it on the controls.

stan_glm(temp3pm ~ temp9am, data = weather_WU, family = gaussian) in Bayes Rules! chapter 11's opening (https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-11), then temp3pm on temp9am and location; weather_WU is this table's Wollongong and Uluru rows, weather_australia %>% filter(location %in% c('Wollongong', 'Uluru')) in the authors' https://github.com/bayes-rules/bayesrules/blob/master/data-raw/weather_WU.Rmd, and the package's R/data_weather_WU.R says 'The weather_australia data in the bayesrules package combines this data with a third city'. No chapter uses weather_australia itself.

exercise 5.13 (Australia) of Bayes Rules! chapter 5 (https://www.bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-5) models the 1000 daily 3 p.m. temperatures temp3pm of weather_perth as Normal around mu with sigma = 5 under a Normal prior and asks for the posterior with summarize_normal_normal(); exercise 10.20 later regresses maxtemp on mintemp, exercise 11.15 asks for a model of temp3pm, and chapter 13 fits logistic regressions of raintomorrow.

Lazic (2008), BMC Physiology 8:16 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2496911), the package author's paper cited as the table's reference: 'the amount of time spent immobile was the main response variable of interest', analysed once as a one-way ANOVA with dose as a factor (Table 2) and once as a linear regression on dose; the help page has no examples and labstats ships no script.

rice.aov <- aov(ShootDryMass ~ trt, data=rice); anova(rice.aov) in the help page's examples ('One and Two-Way Comparisons - Example 4.5'); the authors' Practical Guide code (https://jhmaindonald.github.io/Rcode/R-Code-for--A-Practical-Guide-.-.-.-.pdf, subsection 4.2.1) fits aov(ShootDryMass ~ Block + variety * fert).

RULE GAP: the help page's examples first run princomp on the eleven support scores (columns 9 to 19), then 'regress BDI on the first six principal components', lm(BDI[not.na] ~ ss.pr$scores[, 1:6], data=socsupport), and the authors' Practical Guide code (https://jhmaindonald.github.io/Rcode/R-Code-for--A-Practical-Guide-.-.-.-.pdf) does the same with prcomp and lm(BDI ~ ., data=comp); BDI if a principal component analysis that builds the predictors of the regression that follows is no joint analysis of outcomes, else none (as MASS crabs).

xyplot(log(Time) ~ log(Distance), groups=roadORtrack, data=worldRecords, type=c("p","r")) in the help page's examples draws the least-squares line of log(Time) on log(Distance) per roadORtrack group, after a plain scatterplot and before the loess smooths of type=c("p","smooth").

glm(anvisits ~ gender + factor(income) + factor(travel), family=poisson, data=loomis) in the help page's examples, then glm.nb on the same terms; the details say 'Count models typically use anvisits as response variable'.
titanic$survival <- titanic$survived == 'yes', then glm(survival ~ age + sex + factor(class), family=binomial, data=titanic) in the help page's examples.
glm(AphidCount ~ Field, family = poisson(), data = aphids) in the help page's examples; the description calls AphidCount 'the response variable'.

lm(C ~ Size * Weight * Time, data = biomassc |> transform(Weight = factor(Weight), Time = factor(Time))) and anova(fit) in the help page's examples; the description says 'The response variable recorded was the amount of microbial carbon biomass (C)'.
glm(Conidia ~ Run + (log(Time) + Period) * Source, data = conidia |> transform(Period = factor(Period)), family = poisson()) in the help page's examples.
lm(log(Km) ~ Rep + Voltage, data = voltage) in the help page's examples.
anova(lm(log10(TotalSeed) ~ Site * (HLength + Spikelets), data = weedseed)) in the help page's examples; TotalSeed is the 'Total number of seeds per square meter'.
